caption: The drawing features a rectangular object that appears to be a carved wooden panel, divided evenly into twenty small squares arranged in four columns and five rows. Each square contains a distinct relief carving: the top row depicts a flower, a squirrel, a bird on a branch, and a stork-like bird. The second row shows a swan, a house with trees, a basket of flowers, and a deer or antelope. The third row features two cats playing, a fish, a rabbit or hare, and a bird perched on a branch. In the fourth row, there is a dog sitting, a girl standing in a dress, a horse, and a rooster. The bottom row displays a rose, a cluster of grapes on a vine, a bear standing upright with a staff, and a goat eating grass. The entire panel is rendered in a uniform light brown color, resembling polished wood, against a plain beige background. The name “FRITZ BOEHMER” is printed at the bottom right of the background.
title: Springerle Board for Christmas Cakes
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
